authors: R. Caye Daudt, B. Le Saux, A. Boulch
title: Fully Convolutional Siamese Networks for Change Detection
venue: 25th IEEE International Conference on Image Processing (ICIP), pp. 4063-4067
approach: Three fully convolutional U-Net variants trained end-to-end from scratch: early fusion (FC-EF) and two Siamese designs whose skip connections carry either concatenated (FC-Siam-conc) or absolute-difference (FC-Siam-diff) encoder features.
strength: Small, fast networks with no pre-training requirement; Siamese skip-difference design makes the change signal explicit; became the standard CNN baseline.
limitation: Purely local receptive field from stacked 3x3 convolutions; limited long-range context, so large structures and pseudo-changes (illumination, season) are harder to separate.
relevance: FC-Siam-diff is re-implemented here as the CNN baseline against which the transformer is benchmarked.

authors: R. Caye Daudt, B. Le Saux, A. Boulch, Y. Gousseau
title: Urban Change Detection for Multispectral Earth Observation Using Convolutional Neural Networks
venue: IEEE International Geoscience and Remote Sensing Symposium (IGARSS), pp. 2115-2118
approach: Introduces the Onera Satellite Change Detection (OSCD) dataset of registered Sentinel-2 multispectral image pairs with urban-change labels, and patch-based early-fusion and Siamese CNN classifiers.
strength: First openly available, georeferenced, multispectral benchmark for urban change with a fixed train/test city split.
limitation: Small dataset (24 city pairs) at 10-60 m resolution with coarse, noisy labels; patch-wise classification rather than dense prediction.
relevance: OSCD is the secondary dataset planned for Phase 2 and the reference point for the Sentinel-2 resolution domain gap observed in Phase 1.

title: A Spatial-Temporal Attention-Based Method and a New Dataset for Remote Sensing Image Change Detection
approach: Siamese ResNet feature extractor followed by a spatial-temporal self-attention module (STANet) computed over both dates jointly, trained with a metric (contrastive) loss; releases the LEVIR-CD dataset of 637 very-high-resolution 1024x1024 pairs.
strength: Shows that modelling spatial-temporal dependencies improves robustness to illumination and registration errors; LEVIR-CD provides a large, carefully annotated benchmark with an official split.
limitation: Attention is applied to a single low-resolution CNN feature map and is costly; the dataset covers only building change in Texas, USA, at 0.5 m, limiting geographic and semantic diversity.
relevance: LEVIR-CD (official train/val/test split) is the primary dataset for training and evaluating both models in this project.

authors: S. Fang, K. Li, J. Shao, Z. Li
title: SNUNet-CD: A Densely Connected Siamese Network for Change Detection of VHR Images
venue: IEEE Geoscience and Remote Sensing Letters, vol. 19, pp. 1-5
approach: Combines a Siamese encoder with a densely connected NestedUNet (UNet++) decoder and an ensemble channel attention module to aggregate multi-level semantic features.
strength: Dense skip pathways reduce the loss of fine localisation detail in deep layers, improving boundaries and small-object detection over plain Siamese U-Nets.
limitation: Still convolution-only, so global context is limited; dense connections increase memory use and inference cost.
relevance: Represents the strongest CNN design direction and motivates carrying multi-scale difference features into the decoder, as both of this project's models do.

authors: H. Chen, Z. Qi, Z. Shi
title: Remote Sensing Image Change Detection With Transformers
venue: IEEE Transactions on Geoscience and Remote Sensing, vol. 60, pp. 1-14
approach: Bitemporal Image Transformer (BIT): a ResNet backbone produces features that are compressed into a few semantic tokens per date; a transformer encoder models context over the tokens of both dates and a transformer decoder projects them back to pixel space before feature differencing.
strength: Models long-range space-time context efficiently with a compact token set; better accuracy than purely convolutional baselines at lower computational cost.
limitation: Hybrid design that still depends on a CNN backbone; the transformer operates on a single coarse scale, so there is no hierarchical multi-scale transformer representation.
relevance: Establishes that transformer context modelling helps bitemporal change detection, the hypothesis this project tests with a fully hierarchical Swin encoder.

authors: W. G. C. Bandara, V. M. Patel
title: A Transformer-Based Siamese Network for Change Detection
venue: IEEE International Geoscience and Remote Sensing Symposium (IGARSS), pp. 207-210
topic: Transformer-based satellite change detection / bitemporal fusion
approach: ChangeFormer: a Siamese hierarchical transformer encoder produces multi-scale features for each date; per-scale difference modules feed a lightweight MLP decoder that predicts the change map.
strength: Removes the CNN backbone entirely; multi-scale difference features capture both fine detail and long-range context.
limitation: Trained from scratch-style setups need long schedules and large memory; evaluated on building-centric VHR datasets only.
relevance: Closest architectural relative of this project's model: Siamese hierarchical transformer encoder, per-scale difference fusion and a light decoder.

authors: C. Zhang, L. Wang, S. Cheng, Y. Li
title: SwinSUNet: Pure Transformer Network for Remote Sensing Image Change Detection
venue: IEEE Transactions on Geoscience and Remote Sensing, vol. 60, pp. 1-13
topic: Swin Transformer architectures for change detection
approach: A Siamese U-shaped network built only from Swin Transformer blocks: Siamese Swin encoder, a fusion stage that merges the bitemporal features, and a Swin decoder with patch-expanding upsampling.
strength: Shows that a pure Swin encoder-fusion-decoder can outperform CNN and hybrid models on several change-detection benchmarks.
limitation: Transformer decoder and large backbone make the model heavy for commodity GPUs; evaluated on high-resolution optical benchmarks without cross-sensor or cross-region tests.
relevance: Direct precedent for a Siamese Swin encoder; this project keeps the Swin encoder but uses a convolutional FPN decoder so the model trains and runs within 8 GB of VRAM.

authors: Z. Liu, Y. Lin, Y. Cao, H. Hu, Y. Wei, Z. Zhang, S. Lin, B. Guo
title: Swin Transformer: Hierarchical Vision Transformer using Shifted Windows
venue: IEEE/CVF International Conference on Computer Vision (ICCV), pp. 9992-10002
approach: Hierarchical vision transformer that computes self-attention inside local windows and shifts the window partition between layers to connect neighbouring windows; patch merging builds a four-stage feature pyramid.
strength: Linear complexity in image size and CNN-like multi-scale features, making transformers practical as general backbones for dense prediction.
limitation: Fixed window size ties the model to its training resolution; needs large-scale pre-training to reach its accuracy.
relevance: Provides the hierarchical encoder design used by this project's primary model.

authors: Z. Liu, H. Hu, Y. Lin, Z. Yao, Z. Xie, Y. Wei, J. Ning, Y. Cao, Z. Zhang, L. Dong, F. Wei, B. Guo
title: Swin Transformer V2: Scaling Up Capacity and Resolution
venue: IEEE/CVF Conference on Computer Vision and Pattern Recognition (CVPR), pp. 11999-12009
approach: Residual post-normalisation with scaled cosine attention for training stability and a log-spaced continuous relative position bias that transfers across window sizes and resolutions.
strength: More stable training and better transfer between pre-training and fine-tuning resolutions than Swin V1.
limitation: Gains are demonstrated mostly on natural-image benchmarks; remote-sensing transfer is not studied.
relevance: The exact encoder used here is Swin-V2-Tiny (window 8, 256x256 input), chosen because its pre-training resolution matches the 256x256 tiles.
